name: xecret
description: Open-source, developer-first secret management. Powered by Playxoft.

scripts.// deploy: Always the script, never a bare opennextjs-cloudflare build. The build bakes the deployment's origin into every prerendered canonical, sitemap.xml and robots.txt Host line, and reads it from the environment — which only scripts/deploy-web.sh populates, out of wrangler.toml for the environment being deployed. A build without it publishes localhost. Defaults to production; `npm run deploy -- staging` for the other one.
scripts.// lint: Two configs: eslint.config.mjs covers packages/ and scripts/; apps/web has its own because it needs the Next.js and React rules
scripts.lint: eslint packages scripts && npm run lint --workspaces --if-present
scripts.verify: npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test
scripts.// icons: Regenerates app/icon.svg, favicon.ico and apple-icon.png from the single mark in scripts/generate-icons.ts
scripts.// og: Regenerates public/og.png, the social preview card. Same mark and gradient as the icons above.
scripts.// phase: Phase.dev wrappers, grouped so an editor lists them together. The plain scripts above stay vendor-neutral: CI and self-hosters on Doppler or a .env file run those directly.
scripts.// phase:deploy: Names the Phase environment rather than taking .phase.json's defaultEnv, which is Development. NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_CONFIG is inlined into the client bundle at build time, so the default would ship development's Firebase project inside a production deployment — a build that succeeds and a site nobody can sign in to. deploy-web.sh cross-checks the two and refuses, but the flag is what makes it right rather than merely caught.
scripts.phase:deploy: phase run --env Production -- npm run deploy
scripts.// check:deploy: The preflight. check:env asks whether the values in this shell are sane; this asks whether the Worker that is about to exist will actually have them, by comparing Phase.dev, wrangler.toml and the live Worker. Run it under the environment being deployed -- `npm run phase:check-deploy` does that.
scripts.phase:check-deploy: phase run --env Production -- npm run check:deploy production
